speaker: Unknown
en: When we talk about owning your intelligence, we talk about all of these examples basically building a lot of domain-specific things in and around the models to make it truly best for the domain that you're trying to tackle and really owning your intelligence.

speaker: Unknown
en: And we think there's a few reasons why this has become a phrase that's top of mind for so many people these days.
zh: 而我们认为,这个说法之所以成为如今这么多人最关心的话题,有几个原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: First, token costs are rising a lot.
zh: 第一,token 成本正在大幅上升。

speaker: Unknown
en: People are spending more and more on AI and so as they do so they want to make sure that they're getting the proper ROI and being able to control and monitor token costs is really important and so owning your intelligence in that regard is a key factor.
zh: 人们在 AI 上的花费越来越多,因此他们想确保自己获得合理的 ROI,能够控制和监控 token 成本变得非常重要,所以在这个意义上,拥有你的智能是一个关键因素。

speaker: Unknown
en: Second, we see open models becoming more and more popular.
zh: 第二,我们看到开源模型越来越流行。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this provides not only a really cheap alternative in order to own the token costs more, but it also lets you customize things more.
zh: 这不仅提供了一个非常便宜的替代方案,让你能更好地掌控 token 成本,还让你能做更多定制。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so as these base open weight models get better and better, you can start to post train them, you can start to use them in specialized ways, and that just makes it easier than ever to really own your intelligence.
zh: 随着这些开源权重基础模型越来越好,你可以开始对它们做后训练,可以开始以专门的方式使用它们,这让真正拥有你的智能变得比以往任何时候都更容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the last thing that I think has become pretty clear over the past year is that the models themselves are becoming somewhat commoditized and it's all of this stuff around the model, in particular the data, whether that is actual kind of like context you're providing or some of the domain specific paths that you're baking into the harness,
zh: 然后最后一点,我认为过去一年已经变得相当清楚的是,模型本身正在变得有些商品化,而真正起作用的是围绕模型的这一切,尤其是数据,无论是你提供的实际上下文,还是你烘焙进 harness 里的一些特定领域路径,

speaker: Unknown
en: This is becoming the differentiator to provide a lot of value for folks.
zh: 这正在成为为人们提供大量价值的差异化因素。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so because of all of these factors, we're seeing people want to own their intelligence more and more, and that's how we think about our mission as a company.
zh: 所以由于所有这些因素,我们看到人们越来越想要拥有自己的智能,而这也正是我们思考公司使命的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's always been this way.
zh: 一直都是如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: LangChain got started a month before ChatGPT, but really took off after.
zh: LangChain 的创立比 ChatGPT 早一个月,但真正起飞是在那之后。

speaker: Unknown
en: When people saw that came out, and they were like, I want that, but for my industry, for my vertical,
zh: 当人们看到它问世时,他们说,我想要那个,但要用在我的行业、我的垂直领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then a big value prop of LinkedIn has always been kind of like model optionality.
zh: 而 LangChain 的一大价值主张一直是模型可选性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so from the beginning, people were building these domain-specific things that were naturally kind of like decoupled from the model.
zh: 所以从一开始,人们就在构建这些天然与模型解耦的特定领域的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this mission of kind of like owning intelligence has been something we've thought a lot about.
zh: 所以「拥有智能」这个使命一直是我们深入思考的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we think there's three core pillars to this.
zh: 我们认为这有三个核心支柱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is what we help folks with.
zh: 而这正是我们帮助大家解决的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the first core pillar is open and controllable harness.
zh: 所以第一个核心支柱是开放且可控的 harness。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's two kind of like key parts to this.
zh: 这里面有两个关键部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: One, we think the harness needs to be model neutral, so you shouldn't be coupled to a particular model.
zh: 第一,我们认为 harness 需要是模型中立的,也就是你不应该被耦合到某个特定的模型上。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is both offensive and defensive.
zh: 这既是进攻也是防御。

speaker: Unknown
en: When the best new model comes out, whether it's from OpenAI or Anthropic or TypeSafe with some of their dev models, you want to be able to switch your harness to that as quickly as possible.
zh: 当最好的新模型出现时,无论是来自 OpenAI、Anthropic 还是 TypeSafe 的一些 dev 模型,你希望能够尽快把你的 harness 切换到那个模型上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so your harness needs to be able to adapt to the best new model.
zh: 所以你的 harness 需要能够适应最好的新模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's also defensive.
zh: 这同时也是防御性的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't want to get locked into a single model provider so that they can raise rates and things like that.
zh: 你不希望被锁定在单一模型供应商那里,以至于他们可以随意涨价之类。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other part of this open and controllable harness is, again, what we talked about in terms of making these agents really domain-specific.
zh: 这个开放且可控 harness 的另一部分,还是我们之前谈到的,让这些智能体真正做到领域专用。

speaker: Unknown
en: All of that is about bringing specialized context in particular ways to the model to bring it the right context at the right point in time.
zh: 所有这些都是在以特定方式把专业化的上下文带给模型,在正确的时间点给它正确的上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you need to really control what the harness does.
zh: 而且你需要真正控制 harness 的行为。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what that control looks like could look different for different scenarios.
zh: 这种控制在不同场景下可能看起来不一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we've had LangGraph for a while, which is an open source framework for really creating these directed graphs.
zh: 所以我们已经有 LangGraph 一段时间了,它是一个真正用于创建这些有向图的开源框架。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's a really controllable way of bringing this harness.
zh: 这是一种非常可控的方式来提供这种 harness。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also have deep agents now, and I'll talk about that later, but that's another kind of open source model harness.
zh: 我们现在还有 deep agents,我稍后会讲到,那是另一种开源的模型 harness。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a concept of middleware in there, which is a different way of injecting decisions to make and things to do into this core agentic loop.
zh: 我们里面有一个 middleware 的概念,它是一种不同的方式,用来把要做的决策和要做的事情注入到这个核心的智能体循环里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so regardless of what it is, you need a way to control really in real detail what's going in to the model.
zh: 所以无论它是什么,你都需要一种方式来非常细致地实时控制什么被输入到模型里。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second core pillar that we think makes up owning your intelligence
zh: 我们认为构成拥有你的智能的第二

speaker: Unknown
en: is compounding, specifically compounding the intelligence that you get from when people use your system.
zh: 个核心支柱是复利式增长,具体来说是把你从用户使用系统的过程中获得的智能进行复利式增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when you launch an agent, that is far from having a successful agent.
zh: 所以当你发布一个智能体时,那离拥有一个成功的智能体还很远。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need to learn from how people use the agent, what the agent does, see where it makes mistakes, and being able to compound that agent's intelligence, whether manually by seeing errors and updating the code or updating the prompt,
zh: 你需要从人们如何使用这个智能体、智能体做了什么当中学习,看它在哪里犯错,并能够让这个智能体的智能实现复利式增长,无论是通过人工方式——观察错误并更新代码或更新 prompt——

speaker: Unknown
en: Or more automatically, whether that's with memory or prompt optimization things, this compounding loop is really important to build into your systems and to own.
zh: 还是更自动化的方式,比如用记忆或 prompt 优化之类的工具,这个复利循环非常重要,要构建到你的系统中并由你掌控。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you can define what better and what best looks like for your domain better than anyone else, you will be able to build the best agent for that domain.
zh: 如果你能比任何人都更好地定义对你的领域来说什么更好、什么是最好,你就能为那个领域构建出最好的智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so having evals that define what good looks like and then hill climbing on those evals and compounding that intelligence is a really good way to build these domain-specific agents.
zh: 所以,用 evals 来定义什么算好,然后在这些 evals 上爬山,让智能复利式增长,是构建这些领域专用智能体的非常好的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then lastly, governed.
zh: 最后一个是有治理。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is really crucial for internal agents.
zh: 这对内部智能体来说真的至关重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're seeing a ton of companies transform how they do internal operations, but when you have a lot of agents running around, you need to make sure that they're properly governed.
zh: 我们看到大量公司正在转变它们做内部运营的方式,但当你有很多智能体到处运行时,你需要确保它们得到妥善治理。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need to make sure that you know how many exist, that you can control costs, that you can handle off reliably, so different people accessing it only have access to what they should have access to.
zh: 你需要确保你知道存在多少个智能体,能够控制成本,能够可靠地处理权限,即不同的人访问时只能访问他们应该访问的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we see that governance is becoming an increasingly big topic around owning your intelligence.
zh: 所以我们看到,围绕拥有你的智能,治理正在成为一个越来越大的话题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this is how we think about the three core pillars of owning intelligence.
zh: 这就是我们思考拥有智能的三个核心支柱的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we think there's a bunch of different ways that you can get there.
zh: 我们认为有很多不同的路径可以达到那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so calling three out at a high level, people, process, and technology.
zh: 从高层次举出三个:人员、流程和技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're going to talk most about technology during the rest of the keynote.
zh: 在主题演讲的剩余部分,我们会主要讲技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I want to touch really briefly on people and process, because those are also needed to transform your organization into an organization that can own its intelligence.
zh: 但我想非常简短地谈一下人员和流程,因为要把你的组织转变为一个能够拥有自己智能的组织,这些也是必需的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So touching really briefly on people, this is roughly how we see a lot of organizations being built.
zh: 先非常简短地谈人员,这大致就是我们看到的很多组织的构成方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a ring one of like core platform engineers.
zh: 有一环是核心平台工程师。

speaker: Unknown
en: These provide a lot of tools for other people to build agents.
zh: 他们为其他人构建智能体提供大量工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: When we talk about governance, when we talk about this kind of like eval compounding loop, these provide the platform that other
zh: 当我们谈治理、谈这种 eval 复利循环时,他们提供的是让其他

speaker: Unknown
en: Agent building teams internally can use to build and govern and compound their agents.
zh: 内部智能体构建团队可以用来构建、治理和复利他们的智能体的平台。

speaker: Unknown
en: Outside of that, we see agent engineers.
zh: 在那之外,我们看到的是智能体工程师。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is a great term to describe the weird hybrid mix of data scientist and engineer and machine learning engineer that makes up the people who are driving these agents.
zh: 这是一个很好的术语,用来描述由数据科学家、工程师和机器学习工程师组成的奇怪混合体,正是这些人驱动着这些智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's a new skill set.
zh: 这是一种新的技能组合。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we see a lot of people from different disciplines coming in to be agent engineers, consuming things from the core platform team
zh: 我们看到很多来自不同学科的人进来成为智能体工程师,消费核心平台团队提供的东西

speaker: Unknown
en: And then lastly, there are a ton of subject matter experts inside and outside the company who are often the best people to decide what good looks like for an agent.
zh: 最后,公司内外有大量的领域专家,他们往往是最适合判断智能体什么算好的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so having a platform that can touch those non-developers at the edges is super important.
zh: 所以,拥有一个能够触达这些边缘非开发者的平台超级重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so people and kind of like setting up your organization
zh: 所以人员,以及类似地搭建你的组织

speaker: Unknown
en: Have this type of model is what we see people doing.
zh: 拥有这种类型的模型,就是我们看到大家在做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also see people either implicitly or explicitly adopting a kind of like new process for building agents.
zh: 我们还看到大家在有意或无意地采用一种类似构建智能体的新流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: As I mentioned before, it's very iterative.
zh: 正如我之前提到的,这是非常迭代的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You first launch an agent, it's not going to be good.
zh: 你先发布一个智能体,它不会很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need to iterate.
zh: 你需要迭代。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's this lifecycle, this loop that people are adopting.
zh: 所以就出现了这个生命周期，这个人们正在采用的循环。

speaker: Unknown
en: In order to really get agents to be good enough, roughly speaking, it's build, test, deploy, monitor, and then crucially when you take those monitor learnings and you bring them back into the build step.
zh: 为了真正让智能体变得足够好，大致来说，就是构建、测试、部署、监控，然后关键的是，当你把那些监控所得的经验带回到构建这一步。

speaker: Unknown
en: And of course you want to do all of this in a governed way, and we'll come back to this a little bit later, but people are doing this type of process all the time to improve their agents.
zh: 当然，你会想以受治理的方式完成所有这些，我们稍后会再回到这一点，但人们一直在用这种类型的流程来改进他们的智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I want to talk about the technology.
zh: 接下来我想谈谈技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when we think about the technology and the technology that we help build and provide, there's really like two core parts to it.
zh: 当我们思考技术，以及我们所帮助构建和提供的技术时，它其实有两个核心部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: So one is the runtime.
zh: 一个是运行时。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is how we got started with the open source LangChain libraries and continue to do open source things with LangGraph and DeepAgents.
zh: 这就是我们如何通过开源 LangChain 库起步，并继续用 LangGraph 和 DeepAgents 做开源事情的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, of course, we want to build agents that don't just run locally on your laptop, but run in the cloud and can serve everyone inside your org or the customers that you're building for.
zh: 然后，当然，我们想要构建的智能体不只是在你的笔记本电脑上本地运行，而是在云端运行，可以服务你组织里的所有人，或者你所为之构建的客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's a deployment aspect to this runtime as well.
zh: 所以这个运行时还有一个部署方面的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then there's this observability and evals part, which is really crucial for the compounding layer.
zh: 然后还有可观测性和评估部分，这对复利层来说非常关键。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so being able to see what agents are doing and measure how good they are behaving is really important.
zh: 所以能够看到智能体在做什么，并衡量它们表现得有多好，真的非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: So these are the two core pillars of things that we build.
zh: 这些就是我们构建的东西的两大核心支柱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And recently we've also focused on a third part, which is an intelligence layer that sits above them.
zh: 最近我们还专注于第三部分，也就是位于它们之上的一个智能层。

speaker: Unknown
en: So now when we think about LangSmith, our commercial platform, we think about it serving the runtime aspect, serving the observability evals aspect, and then building an intelligence across the platform to really help people utilize these components and speed up that process, that agent development lifecycle that I talked about earlier.
zh: 所以现在当我们想到 LangSmith，我们的商业化平台时，我们认为它服务于运行时方面，服务于可观测性评估方面，然后在平台之上构建智能，真正帮助人们利用这些组件，加速我之前谈到的那个流程，那个智能体开发生命周期。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so for the next few minutes, I want to walk through these kind of like three core parts of our platform and talk about some of the cool things that we're doing and where we think the future is going.
zh: 所以在接下来的几分钟里，我想走一遍我们平台的这三个核心部分，谈谈我们正在做的一些很酷的事情，以及我们认为未来会走向何方。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I want to start with runtime.
zh: 我想从运行时开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what is the runtime for kind of like an agent look like?
zh: 那么，一个智能体的运行时大致是什么样的？

speaker: Unknown
en: When we think of an agent, we generally think of there being three components.
zh: 当我们想到一个智能体时，我们通常认为它有三个组成部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's the business logic.
zh: 有业务逻辑。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is things like instructions, tools, skills, hooks.
zh: 比如指令、工具、技能、钩子。

speaker: Unknown
en: These are things that you guys have to provide when you're building your domain-specific agents.
zh: 这些是你们在构建领域特定智能体时必须提供的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: What skills for a financial agent might look like are very different than what skills for a legal agent might look like.
zh: 一个金融智能体的技能可能是什么样的，和一个法律智能体的技能可能是什么样的，是非常不同的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this is the business logic that everyone out here will provide to the agents.
zh: 所以这就是在座的每个人都会提供给智能体的业务逻辑。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then there's the harness.
zh: 然后是 harness(执行框架)。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the harness is what takes the model, takes a lot of this domain-specific context, and basically wires it all up so that the model can see the right context at the right point in time.
zh: harness 就是把模型、把很多这种领域特定的上下文，基本上全部接线连接起来，让模型能在正确的时间点看到正确的上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: This can be a very kind of like custom harness that you might build in LangGraph.
zh: 这可以是一个非常自定义的 harness,你可能在 LangGraph 里构建的那种。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or it can be a more kind of like general purpose harness, which we're seeing more and more of.
zh: 或者它可以是一个更通用的 harness,我们正看到越来越多这样的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's why we built DeepAgents.
zh: 这就是为什么我们构建了 DeepAgents。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so DeepAgents is our newest open source library.
zh: DeepAgents 是我们最新的开源库。

speaker: Unknown
en: We launched it about a year ago.
zh: 我们大约一年前发布了它。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's off the shelf agent harness.
zh: 它是一个开箱即用的智能体 harness。

speaker: Unknown
en: It learns a lot from what coding agents do.
zh: 它从编码智能体的做法中学到了很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it has an execution environment with a file system in sandbox.
zh: 所以它有一个带文件系统和沙箱的执行环境。

speaker: Unknown
en: It does a lot of context management in ways that coding agents do it with compaction.
zh: 它用压缩的方式做了大量上下文管理，就像编码智能体做的那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's built so that you can build these domain specific agents.
zh: 但它的构建目的是让你可以构建这些领域特定的智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then lastly, there's the infrastructure.
zh: 最后，还有基础设施。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you take this agent and it's running locally on your laptop, great.
zh: 如果你把这个智能体拿到你的笔记本电脑上本地运行，很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: You want to bring it to the cloud.
zh: 你想把它带到云端。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's all of these components that you're going to need to add in so that it can run remotely.
zh: 那么你需要添加所有这些组件，才能让它远程运行。

speaker: Unknown
en: You'll want a runtime in a server that has durable execution.
zh: 你会想要一个服务器里具有持久执行能力的运行时。

speaker: Unknown
en: You'll want some way to access tools securely.
zh: 你会想要某种安全访问工具的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: You'll want some way to run this code that it writes.
zh: 你会想要某种运行它所写代码的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we see a lot of agents writing code, even if they're not coding agents.
zh: 我们看到很多智能体在写代码，即使它们不是编码智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: You'll need to access models.
zh: 你需要访问模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's all this infrastructure that goes into it as well.
zh: 所以还有所有这些基础设施要加入进来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so these are a lot of the components that we've built into LangSmith in pieces.
zh: 而这些就是我们分部分构建进 LangSmith 的很多组件。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we have LangSmith deployments.
zh: 我们有 LangSmith deployments。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's really around the agent runtime.
zh: 那主要是围绕智能体运行时的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have LangSmith sandboxes for running codes.
zh: 我们有 LangSmith sandboxes 用于运行代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: In beta, we have an LLM gateway in LangSmith, and I'll talk about that, but that's for access to models.
zh: 在 beta 中,我们在 LangSmith 里有一个 LLM 网关,我会讲到这个,但那是用于访问模型的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then a tool server is something that we're working on for easy access to tools.
zh: 然后工具服务器是我们正在开发的东西,用于方便地访问工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's these different components that make up the infrastructure.
zh: 所以有这些不同的组件构成了基础设施。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of the things that we launched in beta at last interrupt, but I want to spotlight real quick, is managed deep agents.
zh: 而我们在上次 interrupt 的 beta 中发布的东西之一,但我想快速重点介绍一下,是 managed deep agents。

speaker: Unknown
en: So managed deep agents basically takes this harness and the managed infrastructure and combines it into one.
zh: 所以 managed deep agents 基本上是把这个 harness 和托管基础设施结合成一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so now when you're building an agent,
zh: 所以现在当你构建一个智能体时,

speaker: Unknown
en: You just provide your business logic and then you get the harness and managed infrastructure together.
zh: 你只需提供你的业务逻辑,然后你就把 harness 和托管基础设施一起拿到了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's a lot easier to get started with than having to go business logic to harness to assembling all these three or four or five different pieces of infrastructure.
zh: 所以这比必须走业务逻辑到 harness 再到组装这三四五个不同的基础设施部件要容易上手得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we're really, really excited about the managed deep agents platform as a way to accelerate time to value and speed to kind of like production for a lot of these agents.
zh: 所以我们对 managed deep agents 平台感到非常非常兴奋,把它作为加速这些智能体的价值实现时间和进入生产速度的一种方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a few things that we're announcing today as part of a new Managed Deep Agents release that we think will help even more with this.
zh: 今天我们作为新的 Managed Deep Agents 发布的一部分宣布了一些东西,我们认为这将在这方面提供更大帮助。

speaker: Unknown
en: So first, one of the hardest parts of building these, especially internal company agents, is auth and making sure that the right people can access and use the agent, but also that when they use the agent, if the agent connects to Notion or Jira,
zh: 那么首先,构建这些东西最困难的部分之一,尤其是公司内部智能体,是认证,确保正确的人能够访问和使用智能体,同时当他们使用智能体时,如果智能体连接到 Notion 或 Jira,

speaker: Unknown
en: It's connecting either on behalf of the user or as the agent's kind of fixed set of identity.
zh: 它是以用户身份连接,还是以智能体那种固定的身份集合连接。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then what the right answer is might depend.
zh: 而正确答案是什么可能要视情况而定。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we're introducing a lot of different primitives in managed deep agents to facilitate this type of connections.
zh: 所以我们在 managed deep agents 中引入了很多不同的原语来促成这种类型的连接。

speaker: Unknown
en: So first is connections.
zh: 首先是 connections(连接)。

speaker: Unknown
en: These are basically tools.
zh: 这些基本上就是工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you have a tool server, which is how Managed Deep Agents connects to tools, you can specify how you want your end users to auth to those connections.
zh: 当你有一个工具服务器,也就是 Managed Deep Agents 连接工具的方式,你可以指定你希望终端用户如何对这些连接进行认证。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're using auth there.
zh: 所以我们在那里使用了认证。

speaker: Unknown
en: Related to that, we have this idea of identity for agents.
zh: 与此相关,我们有这个智能体身份的概念。

speaker: Unknown
en: This just defines the agent to be either user-permissioned or service-permissioned on a whole.
zh: 这只是把智能体整体定义为用户权限还是服务权限。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then third is channels.
zh: 然后第三是 channels(通道)。

speaker: Unknown
en: So a big part of building these agents is exposing them to people.
zh: 所以构建这些智能体的一个重要部分是把它们暴露给人们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Slack is a massive one.
zh: Slack 是一个巨大的渠道。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you have agents in Slack,
zh: 当你在 Slack 中有智能体时,

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you deal with auth in like a shared channel?
zh: 你如何处理共享频道中的认证?

speaker: Unknown
en: If I message it in a shared public channel and my coworker messages it, whose auth does it use?
zh: 如果我在一个共享的公共频道里给它发消息,而我的同事也给它发消息,它用谁的认证?

speaker: Unknown
en: For which runs?
zh: 对于哪些运行?

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of that we're baking in to off-the-shelf channels and manage deep agents to hopefully make the auth problem a lot easier.
zh: 我们把其中很多都内置到了现成的通道和 managed deep agents 中,希望让认证问题变得容易得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Second, we're adding more things around memory into managed deep agents.
zh: 第二,我们正在向 managed deep agents 添加更多关于记忆的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so managed deep agents has always had a concept of agent level memory, but we're now adding in user level memory.
zh: 所以 managed deep agents 一直有智能体级别记忆的概念,但我们现在正在加入用户级别记忆。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this means that it can remember things specific to the individual users that it interacts with.
zh: 所以这意味着它可以记住与它交互的个别用户所特有的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is really powerful for customizing agents.
zh: 这对于定制智能体来说非常强大。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then third, we're adding in built-in tools.
zh: 然后第三,我们正在加入内置工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: So one of the most common things that agents need to do is search the web.
zh: 所以智能体需要做的最常见的事情之一就是搜索网络。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we're adding in a built-in tool via parallel so that agents can access the web.
zh: 所以我们正在通过 parallel 加入一个内置工具,让智能体可以访问网络。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so now you no longer have to go get a separate API key for that.
zh: 所以现在你不再需要为此去获取一个单独的 API 密钥。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can just use your LangSmith API key, use it with managed deep agents, and get access to the parallel web search MCP.
zh: 你只需使用你的 LangSmith API 密钥,配合 managed deep agents 使用,就可以访问 parallel 网络搜索 MCP。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so putting this all together, managed deep agents we think is the easiest way to go from the business logic to an agent that's actually running in production.
zh: 把这些放在一起,我们认为 managed deep agents 是从业务逻辑到一个真正在生产中运行的智能体的最简单方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've been working with a number of early design partners on this, and we've seen really good results, especially for just getting an agent up and running and having it be like this company harness.
zh: 我们一直在与许多早期设计合作伙伴就此合作,我们看到了非常好的结果,尤其是在让一个智能体快速启动运行,并让它成为这种公司 harness 方面。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's how we think about managed deep agents, is this company harness that makes it really easy to get started building and sharing agents inside an org.
zh: 这就是我们如何看待 managed deep agents 的,它是这个公司 harness,让在一个组织内部构建和共享智能体变得非常容易上手。

speaker: Unknown
en: The next thing in the runtime that I want to spotlight is decision models.
zh: 运行时中我想重点介绍的下一件事是 decision models(决策模型)。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so over the weekend, I, as I'm sure many of you did, played around with Jev.
zh: 所以在周末,我,我相信你们中的很多人也一样,玩了一下 Jev。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it launched over the weekend.
zh: 所以它是在周末发布的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a really interesting new type of model.
zh: 它是一种非常有趣的新型模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what exactly is Jev?
zh: 那么 Jev 到底是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a decision model.
zh: 它是一个决策模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: What does that mean?
zh: 这是什么意思?

speaker: Unknown
en: It basically means that it makes decisions.
zh: 它基本上意味着它做决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: You send it a state.
zh: 你给它发送一个状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: You send it a list of questions.
zh: 你给它发送一个问题列表。

speaker: Unknown
en: It can then score those questions.
zh: 然后它可以对这些问句进行评分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's different things that you can have it score on.
zh: 而且可以让它针对不同的方面进行评分。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it can either be like a Boolean or an actual score or a categorical choice.
zh: 所以可以是布尔值，也可以是实际的分数，或者是一个分类选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it basically makes decisions.
zh: 但它基本上就是做决策的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It can't generate text, but it can make decisions.
zh: 它不能生成文本，但它可以做决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so even though it's more limited, we think this is really interesting.
zh: 所以尽管它更受限，我们认为这非常有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: We think there are a bunch of different types of models and a bunch of different types of agent harnesses that will be built.
zh: 我们认为会有很多不同类型的模型和很多不同类型的智能体框架被构建出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we think absolutely there will be these frontier models that are driving these really complex harnesses.
zh: 所以我们绝对认为，会有这些驱动非常复杂框架的前沿模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's what you're going to use in Claude Code and Codex and DeepAgents.
zh: 而这就是你将在 Claude Code、Codex 和 DeepAgents 中使用的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: These take advantage.
zh: 这些利用了

speaker: Unknown
en: of these really frontier models.
zh: 这些非常前沿的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there's also a ton of other decisions that need to be made, and that's where we think a decision model can be really helpful.
zh: 但还有大量其他需要做出的决策，而我们正是因此认为决策模型会非常有用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And maybe these are small things that actually go along with the frontier model, or maybe they empower the lane graph cognitive architectures and routing between different things.
zh: 也许它们是一些与前沿模型配套的小东西，或者它们能赋能 lane graph 认知架构以及不同事物之间的路由。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so calling out a few of the things that we think these decision models are really useful, one is evals, so either running after the fact or in the loop.
zh: 那么列举几个我们认为这些决策模型真正有用的场景，其一是评估，也就是事后运行或在循环中运行。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you have an agent doing work, if you can score it quickly,
zh: 如果你有一个智能体在工作，如果你能快速对它评分，

speaker: Unknown
en: According to some criteria as it's running, that's really powerful because then you can catch mistakes in real time.
zh: 按照某些标准在它运行时进行评分，那会非常强大，因为这样你就能实时发现错误。

speaker: Unknown
en: Two, guardrails.
zh: 其二，护栏。

speaker: Unknown
en: So flagging user input really fast.
zh: 也就是非常快速地标记用户输入。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I was talking to some people yesterday and we were talking about guardrails.
zh: 我昨天和一些人在聊，我们在谈护栏。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the downsides of guardrails is that it always adds latency.
zh: 护栏的一个缺点是它总会增加延迟。

speaker: Unknown
en: If now we can add them in a really low latency way, that's really cool and powerful.
zh: 如果现在我们能以非常低延迟的方式加入护栏，那会非常酷、非常强大。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we're excited about it for that.
zh: 所以我们为此感到兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then lastly, model routing as well.
zh: 最后，还有模型路由。

speaker: Unknown
en: Choosing which agents or which models or which skills or tools to load.
zh: 选择加载哪些智能体、哪些模型、哪些技能或工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: We think things like Jev will be really, really useful for that.
zh: 我们认为像 JEV 这样的东西会对此非常有用。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you can access JEV through the LangSmith LLM gateway.
zh: 你可以通过 LangSmith LLM 网关访问 JEV。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can also access an open source decision model that we're hosting there called semif.
zh: 你也可以访问一个我们在那里托管的开源决策模型，叫 semif。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's been a massive explosion in these open source decision models since JEV launched.
zh: 自从 JEV 发布以来，这些开源决策模型出现了大规模爆发。

speaker: Unknown
en: We think this is a new type of model that there will absolutely be a lot of options for, and we're really, really excited to power and host a lot of these through our gateway.
zh: 我们认为这是一种新型的模型，绝对会有很多选择，而我们非常、非常兴奋能通过我们的网关为其中很多提供支持和托管。

speaker: Unknown
en: Speaking really quickly of our gateway, this is the last thing in the runtime that I want to spotlight.
zh: 快速说一下我们的网关，这是我想在运行时部分重点介绍的最后一件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we launched LangSmith's LLM gateway in beta about a month or two ago.
zh: 我们在大约一两个月前以测试版的形式发布了 LangSmith 的 LLM 网关。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's two main things that I want to highlight.
zh: 有两个主要的东西我想强调一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: One, we try to make it so that the gateway can be used in all of the LLM applications that you're building, whether they are customer-facing or internal.
zh: 其一，我们努力让这个网关可以被用于你正在构建的所有 LLM 应用，无论它们是面向客户的还是内部的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So specifically, we normalize everything through OpenAI and actually Anthropic message format.
zh: 具体来说，我们把所有东西都规范化为 OpenAI 以及 Anthropic 的消息格式。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you can access it there.
zh: 所以你可以通过它访问。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we also allow straight pass-through in case there are new features that come out in these APIs and you just want to take advantage of.
zh: 但我们也允许直接透传，以防这些 API 推出你只想直接利用的新功能。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we also have a bunch of coding agent integrations.
zh: 我们还有一堆编码智能体的集成。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Codex and Claude Code and Cursor, again, we think you should be routing all of your traffic for governance and cost control reasons.
zh: 所以 Codex、Claude Code 和 Cursor——我们再次认为，出于治理和成本控制的原因，你应该把所有流量都路由

speaker: Unknown
en: We think you should be routing all of it through a single element gateway.
zh: 到一个统一的网关。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that means it needs to integrate with every application that's using AI.
zh: 而这意味着它需要与每一个使用 AI 的应用集成。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we want to make it so really easy to plug into all of those.
zh: 所以我们希望让接入这些应用变得非常容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the main kind of like features that we're focusing on, one is cost controls, having cost visibility but also setting spend limits for different teams, different users, different API keys.
zh: 然后我们重点关注的几类功能，其一是成本控制，既要有成本可见性，也要能为不同团队、不同用户、不同 API 密钥设置消费限额。

speaker: Unknown
en: Two is rate limiting, so making sure that there's not a single application that's really throttling or taking up a lot of usage there.

en: And then third is fallbacks.

en: So you can fall back to different model providers when you get an error.

en: So if you notice that requests are failing and Anthropic might be down, you don't even try them for the future.
